chunks: And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said:

Allah (Glorified is His Majesty) has said: Among My believing servants are those whose religious affairs are not set right except by wealth, affluence, and health in the body; so I test them with wealth, affluence, and health in the body, and their religious affairs become set right.

And He said: Among the servants are those whose religious affairs are not set right except by poverty, destitution, and illness in their bodies; so I test them with poverty, destitution, and illness in their bodies, and their religious affairs become set right for them.
ai.seo_question: How do wealth and poverty both serve to perfect a believer's religion according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes how God tests His believing servants through two different conditions: wealth and health, or poverty and illness. In both cases, the specific condition serves as a means to rectify and perfect their religious affairs, implying that neither prosperity nor hardship is inherently detrimental to faith if it leads to spiritual improvement.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 37. Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) narrated that the Prophet (a.s) said:

Allah [M.G] has said: Amongst My believing servants there are those whose religious affairs are not set right except by wealth, affluence and health; so, I give them these as their lot that the affairs of their religion may be set right.

And amongst the servants there are those whose religious affairs are not set right except by hunger, poverty and disease; so, I afflict them with hunger, poverty and disease so that the affairs of their religion may be set right for them.
